summary: Verified the network-rail visibility fix via IntersectionObserver on the homepage across all sections and on /work and /contact routes. Rail is correctly hidden on hero, clients, contact, footer, and non-homepage routes; visible in the network section. Bug is FIXED.

issues: At the exact scroll position where purpose section starts (block:'start'), a ~31px sliver of the network section remains in view and the rail still shows opacity=1. As soon as the user scrolls further (+400px into purpose), rail correctly fades to opacity=0. This is a minor boundary edge from IntersectionObserver threshold 0.02 and not a real UX defect (the network section is still technically visible). If desired, main agent could tighten threshold or also gate via section index/scroll offset to fade the rail slightly earlier.

test_results_table.purpose_start: opacity 1 (boundary: 31px of network still in viewport) - acceptable

critical_code_review_comments: IntersectionObserver threshold 0.02 means the rail stays visible until <2% of the (very tall, 3600px) network section is intersecting. That's up to ~72px sliver keeping rail visible. If tighter fade-out is desired at section boundary, consider using rootMargin (e.g. '-10% 0px -10% 0px') or a scroll-position-based check as backup.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (8/8 required checks passing; 1 non-blocking boundary observation)

context_for_next_testing_agent: The bug fix is verified. .network-rail correctly hidden outside the network section on the homepage and not rendered on /work and /contact routes. Only a boundary edge exists at exact top-of-purpose scroll due to threshold 0.02 — acceptable and non-blocking.
rca of the issue: Original: .network-rail was position:fixed opacity:1 always → showed on every section. Fix: IntersectionObserver toggles 'network-experience--in-view' on <section id='network'>; CSS gates opacity/pointer-events. Verified working across all sections and routes.
